key_insight: ShotStream reframes multi-shot video generation as next-shot prediction conditioned on historical context, enabling a causal streaming architecture that supports low-latency, interactive on-the-fly frame generation.
problem_solved: Addresses the limited interactivity and high latency of bidirectional multi-shot video models by allowing users to dynamically steer an ongoing narrative and receive immediate frame/shot outputs without reprocessing the entire video.
method: Reformulate multi-shot generation as next-shot generation conditioned on a compact history buffer and streaming user prompts.
Design a causal multi-shot architecture that generates shots sequentially (shot-by-shot) rather than via bidirectional passes, enabling incremental decoding and state caching.
Optimize for on-the-fly synthesis with efficient sampling and cached state updates so new instructions can be applied mid-story with low latency.
impact: Enables real-time, user-in-the-loop storytelling workflows (games, live content creation, interactive narratives) by reducing latency and improving interactivity for long-form video generation. Practitioners can build responsive generative systems that adapt to dynamic prompts without full re-generation.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: historical shots → streaming prompt → next-shot generation (illustrates causality and incremental updates).
Architecture block diagram: history buffer, causal generator, prompt interface, state cache (shows dataflow and where low-latency gains arise).
Latency vs. interactivity chart: ShotStream vs. bidirectional baselines (throughput, average response time).
UI mockup: live prompt panel controlling an ongoing video timeline (demonstrates interactive storytelling experience).
paper_title: ShotStream: Streaming Multi-Shot Video Generation for Interactive Storytelling
paper_authors: Yawen Luo, Xiaoyu Shi, Junhao Zhuang, Yutian Chen, Quande Liu
